title: Kahana vs Circle: Keep the Chat, Add the Shelf

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

Feature set expanded to include Android app, courses, automated workflows, live events, and AI features.

strengths.title: Community-first, workspace-style model
strengths.detail: Feels like Slack/Discord but optimized for communities: spaces, topics, posts, live sessions, and chat.

strengths.title: Integrated courses, events, and live streaming
strengths.detail: Host courses, livestreams, and events inside the platform alongside structured discussion.

strengths.title: Monetization tools and paywalls
strengths.detail: Built-in paywalls and membership tiers for free communities and paid memberships/content.

strengths.title: Automation and engagement tools
strengths.detail: Automation builder for onboarding, tagging, and workflows; polls, challenges, quizzes, and gamification.

weaknesses.title: Higher cost vs simpler platforms
weaknesses.detail: USD 89+/month plus transaction fees, more expensive than Discord/Telegram; cost is a recurring complaint.

weaknesses.title: UI can feel cluttered
weaknesses.detail: Many options and spaces can overwhelm; onboarding non-tech members can be challenging.

weaknesses.title: Landing page customization limited
weaknesses.detail: Native landing builder has limited design control; many creators still use external tools for high-conversion pages.

weaknesses.title: Transaction fees on all plans
weaknesses.detail: Platform fees (4%–0.5%) stack on Stripe/processor fees and can hit margins.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Circle is branded community spaces, courses, posts, events, and member chat for creators running a paid or free community. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Circle is a powerful, all-in-one community platform for creators, coaches, and businesses, customized communities with structured discussions, courses, streamed events, and live chat.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Circle side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Circle you can use Courses, Memberships, and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Circle

You can use both. Circle keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Circle. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
